name: hide the rule and ask which one it was
one_line: Take a form that applies a stated rule, run it, print what came out and delete the rule, then ask which rule it was.
how: It applies wherever something on the page was generated by a rule with a setting in it — a base, a step size, a starting row, a number in a table. Run it yourself, print the result, take the setting out, and ask for it back. Then print the one line that makes it check itself: put your answer in, run the rule again, and see whether the same thing comes out. Print enough of the result to leave exactly one possible answer, which is a count somebody has to do before printing and not a feeling, and print no more than that, because every further line is one less thing left to work out.

knobs.knob: how much of the result is shown
knobs.effect: five rows of a three-cell grid rule leave one candidate out of two hundred and fifty-six; two rows leave sixteen and the question has no answer. Where that line falls has to be counted, and it differs for every rule.

knobs.knob: whether the rule is hidden or one of its outputs
knobs.effect: hiding the rule asks about the whole run at once; hiding one output asks for the rule to be applied one more time, which is exactly what the form already was before the move touched it.
one line saying to put the answer back and run it again turns a guess into something that settles itself; without that line the sheet has to be marked by somebody who knows the answer.

where_the_work_is: In how much gets printed. The move itself costs one deletion; whether it works at all is decided entirely by the amount of the run left on the page, and that has to be counted before anything is handed over.
breaks: It only works on forms whose rule has a setting that could have been otherwise — a rule with no parameter has nothing to take out. Where the run is slow to develop, printing enough of it to pin the answer down can cost more of the page than the form did.
